title: Reset Hard Readback
summary: Lists exactly what git reset --hard, clean, checkout -- . or stash drop would destroy, and offers to stash first.
description: Readback for destructive git commands from porcelain status: edited files with +/- lines, staged new files, untracked and ignored files (.env and keys first), commits the branch moves past with unpushed ones marked, stash ids to recover, what stays, and a stash-first option.
catches: Tracked edits that would be discarded, with +/- line counts
Staged new files and untracked/ignored files, secrets like .env and keys listed first
Commits the branch would move past, with unpushed ones marked
Stash entries dropped, with the sha to recover them
What the command leaves alone (e.g. submodules without --recurse-submodules)
limits: Only as complete as the status, numstat, commits and stashes you pass
Parses common forms of reset, clean, checkout/restore and stash drop; unusual flags may not be modelled
Does not run git; onStash and onConfirm are yours
a11y: Each loss group is a section labelled by its heading; the list is a labelled group
Long groups expand with a button instead of truncating silently
Confirm receives focus when the readback opens; buttons set aria-busy while pending
server: In tooling that runs these commands for users, keep a reflog/backup and require explicit confirmation server-side; this component only describes the loss.
stops: Uncommitted work wiped by git reset
mistakes: git reset hard lost my changes
